I the only one who feels that Flansham Park Surgery has deteriorated significantly since the pandemic?
The automated phone service now seems designed to make you want to go elsewhere. You'd think it was a busy London hospital, when clearly it's probably just one person answering the calls in the back office.
I suffer from severe mental health issues. My condition means I face negative and dark thoughts daily, and yet, due to the lack of funding in the Arun district, (as explained by Flansham Park) and unable to see a professional, I am left to deal with these challenges on my own. The surgery used to be a place of refuge, where, on rare occasions, I could turn to a GP when things became unbearable. However, since the pandemic, it feels as though the GPs have simply disappeared. The new system they've implemented doesn't seem to be there to help—it seems to be more about deterring people from even attempting to see a doctor.

I tried to make an appointment using their online system, as suggested during the automated call, but the process was frustratingly useless. The prompts lead you down irrelevant paths, asking questions that don't even address your real concerns. It's disheartening that in this day and age, when my mental health is in such a fragile state, the process of trying to get an appointment only serves to worsen my thoughts.

Over the past six years, when I have managed to get an appointment, 80% of the time I have been redirected to a paramedic whose only role is to pass my details on to a doctor.
